correctness.rationale: All real projections can be averaged over dihedral signed edge isometries. Every invariant projection is represented by a reflection-antisymmetric cyclic convolution column a, with exact spoke/rim l1 column norms S(a),T(a). An explicit two-supported a achieves F(t) precisely when its rim kernel total-variation branch has u<=1/3 (t<=t_star). An explicit five-entry q and positive convex combination give the lower bound F(t)+[t(3-2t)/(1+2t+2t²)]sum_{j>=1}|a_j| for 0<t<3/2. Equality outside the interval forces forbidden total variation, establishing strictness. The smaller wheels have independent explicit strict upper bounds. The standard-library exact checker passed 520 rational in-range cases plus 30 small wheels; a separate unrestricted full-projection linear program passed 20 cases. Finite tests corroborate, but the algebraic certificate is the proof. No statement about t>=3/2 is made.

value.rationale: The exact minimal projection norm of an m-dimensional wheel cycle subspace in a 2m-dimensional weighted edge l1 space is a natural Banach complementability invariant and the parametric problem is not settled by an unweighted value. The finding identifies a uniform nontrivial interval independent of graph size, an algebraic obstruction threshold t_star and a sharp minimal rim count of six. The boundary follows from a structural five-edge dual witness and detects a genuine change in the active norm constraint; it is not a renaming or a routine increment of an old number. It does not require a downstream theorem for this structural extremal classification to be useful.
